The transformer idioms `evoxc` does not ship, as graph→graph compositions.

`evoxc` deliberately owns no NN layers: it has no `softmax`, `layer_norm`,
`rms_norm`, `silu`, top-level `where`, `rsqrt` or `iota`. Everything in
this module is therefore a *composition* of public `evoxc` ops built on
`SymbolicTensor` values — there is no eager numerical path here, and no new IR
op. Calling these functions with concrete tensors is the same user error as
calling `evoxc.add` on a concrete tensor (an `evoxc.TraceError` from the
underlying op), which is exactly the intended explicitness.

Shape/dtype policy
------------------
Every helper is **static-shape only**: where a helper needs an extent to build a
`reshape`/`slice`, it reads it from the operand's static shape and raises
`evoxc_hf.errors.HFUnsupportedError` naming the offending axis if that dim
is symbolic (`Dim`/`DimExpr`). Nothing is ever guessed from a dynamic dim,
and no helper silently falls back to a Python loop. Cost: one graph per concrete
shape (the package-wide static-shape-first contract). Dtypes are whatever the
operands are — every helper preserves the input floating dtype; there is no
implicit cast.

RoPE tables: in-graph, not host inputs
-------------------------------------
`rope_cos_sin` computes the `(seq_len, head_dim)` cos/sin tables **inside
the graph** from `arange` + `power` + `cos`/`sin` (all StableHLO-exportable
in v1) rather than taking them as extra graph inputs. This deliberately differs
from a host-precomputed-tables design and was chosen because it:

* keeps the graph signature at `(params, input_ids)` — no extra positional
  inputs the caller could forget to supply, and nothing to keep in sync when the
  sequence length changes;
* keeps the emitted program's op count independent of `seq_len` (the tables are
  a rank-1 iota expansion, not a payload);
* avoids an `evoxc.constant` payload, which is the one explicit-but-warned way to
  embed data (`evoxc.constant` inlines the bytes into MLIR text);

and was measured bit-comparable to HuggingFace's own f32 tables. The host
equivalent `rope_tables` is exposed for the pure-numpy reference oracle and
for reporting; it produces the same numbers via the same formula.

Export safety
-------------
Exact erf-GELU (`gelu_erf`, i.e. `hidden_act` `"gelu"` / `"erf"`)
uses `evoxc.erf`, a documented **v1 StableHLO export deferral**: such a graph
still traces, compiles and runs on the numpy interpreter backend, but any
compiler backend rejects it with an explicit `evoxc.BackendError`. Configs that
select it are flagged through `EXPORT_UNSAFE_ACTIVATIONS` /
`activation_is_export_safe` so the model builders can refuse the compiled
path up front instead of failing deep inside lowering.

## Symbols

- [`activation_is_export_safe`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/activation-is-export-safe/) — Whether a graph built with this activation can be lowered to StableHLO.
- [`apply_rope`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/apply-rope/) — Rotate `(batch, heads, seq, head_dim)` queries/keys with HF `rotate_half`.
- [`causal_mask`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/causal-mask/) — In-graph `(seq_len, seq_len)` f32 additive causal mask.
- [`gelu_erf`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/gelu-erf/) — Exact erf-GELU: `0.5x(1 + erf(x / sqrt(2)))`.
- [`gelu_tanh`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/gelu-tanh/) — `gelu_new` / `gelu_pytorch_tanh`: `0.5x(1 + tanh(sqrt(2/pi)(x + 0.044715x^3)))`.
- [`layer_norm`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/layer-norm/) — HF `nn.LayerNorm`: biased variance over the **last** axis.
- [`merge_heads`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/merge-heads/) — `(b, n_heads, s, head_dim) -> (b, s, n_heads * head_dim)`.
- [`repeat_kv`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/repeat-kv/) — GQA/MQA expansion: `(b, n_kv, s, hd) -> (b, n_kv * n_rep, s, hd)`.
- [`resolve_activation`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/resolve-activation/) — Map an HF activation name to its graph-building activation function.
- [`rms_norm`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/rms-norm/) — HF `LlamaRMSNorm`: `weight * x * (1 / sqrt(mean(x^2, -1, keepdims) + eps))`.
- [`rope_cos_sin`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/rope-cos-sin/) — In-graph `(seq_len, head_dim)` f32 RoPE `(cos, sin)` tables.
- [`rope_tables`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/rope-tables/) — Host-side numpy f32 RoPE `(cos, sin)` tables — the reference oracle.
- [`silu`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/silu/) — SiLU / swish: `x * sigmoid(x)`.
- [`softmax`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/softmax/) — Numerically stable softmax over `axis`: `exp(x - max) / sum(exp(x - max))`.
- [`split_heads`](/api/evoxc-hf/ops/split-heads/) — `(b, s, n_heads * head_dim) -> (b, n_heads, s, head_dim)`.
